newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala government suspends peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala government suspends peace talks.

text.p: The Guatemalan government said on Monday it was suspending peace talks with the country's leftist URNG guerrillas planned for Tuesday in Mexico, saying the recent kidnapping of a woman by the rebels had violated the terms of the negotiations.

"This is a violation of the human rights accord and a violation of the fundamentals of the negotiation process and the negotiations scheduled for tomorrow are suspended until we get a full explanation from the URNG," Interior Minister Rodolfo Mendoza told a news conference.
Mendoza told reporters it was essential for the credibility of the talks to suspend the negotiating process until the URNG had given a full explanation. He did not give further details of the kidnap.
The government had been due to meet the URNG, the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit, in Mexico City on Tuesday for a final round of peace talks, focusing this time on the URNG's future status.

The two sides have been negotiating an end to Guatemala's 35-year-old civil war on and off under United Nations auspices since 1991. The talks gained a new momentum this year when a ceasefire was agreed, and a final agreement was expected by December.
In September, the rebels and the government signed a landmark agreement to cut Guatemala's powerful army by a third.
